purpose: SlicerSPINEPS integrates the SPINEPS whole-spine segmentation pipeline into 3D Slicer to segment MRI (T2w, T1w, Vibe) and CT spine volumes into anatomical per-vertebra instance masks and semantic subregion masks. It provides both a graphical module for clinicians and researchers and a reusable Python library interface for other Slicer modules.
summary:
SlicerSPINEPS is a well-engineered and thoroughly documented extension for whole-spine MRI and CT segmentation using SPINEPS, running inference out-of-process and carefully pinning Slicer's bundled packages (`SimpleITK`, `numpy`, `scipy`) during dependency installation. No safety or licensing issues were found. However, under the Slicer Extensions Index review policy, installing PyTorch directly via `light-the-torch` without declaring and using the Slicer `PyTorch` extension (`PyTorchUtils` in `EXTENSION_DEPENDS` and `build_dependencies`) is a blocking environment issue. Additionally, there is a minor non-blocking mismatch in `test_ParameterArgList` where assertions check for outdated single-dash CLI flags.

🔴 Do not merge yet: PyTorch must be installed via the Slicer `PyTorch` extension (`PyTorchUtils` and `build_dependencies` / `EXTENSION_DEPENDS`) rather than directly invoking `light-the-torch`.

safety.rationale: Inspected all 10 text files in the repository (`CMakeLists.txt`, `SlicerSPINEPS/CMakeLists.txt`, `SlicerSPINEPS/SlicerSPINEPS.py`, all files in `SlicerSPINEPS/SlicerSPINEPSLib/`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`). There is no telemetry, unauthorized network transmission, unsafe deserialization, command injection (`QProcess` and `subprocess.run` are used without a shell and with argument lists), or prompt injection.

environment.rationale: Inspected `SlicerSPINEPS/SlicerSPINEPSLib/InstallLogic.py` and `CMakeLists.txt`. No packages are installed at import or startup, and user confirmation is requested before installing dependencies, with constraints pinning `SimpleITK`, `numpy`, `scipy`, `torch`, and `nnunetv2`. However, `InstallLogic._installTorch` installs PyTorch directly via `light-the-torch` instead of using the Slicer `PyTorch` extension (`PyTorchUtils`), which violates the Extensions Index policy.

packaging.rationale: Inspected `CMakeLists.txt`, `SlicerSPINEPS/CMakeLists.txt`, and the catalog entry. All Python scripts and icon resources exist and are properly listed in `SlicerSPINEPS/CMakeLists.txt`, and no large binary weights are committed to the repository.

license.rationale: Inspected `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, and `README.md`. The extension is clearly licensed under Apache-2.0, with proper attribution in `NOTICE` to SlicerNNUnet, SlicerTotalSegmentator, and upstream SPINEPS (also Apache-2.0), and clear explanations regarding dynamically downloaded upstream model weights.

soundness.rationale: Inspected `SlicerSPINEPS/SlicerSPINEPS.py` and `SlicerSPINEPS/SlicerSPINEPSLib/*.py`. The architecture is clean and well-thought-out, running inference in an unbuffered `QProcess` off the GUI thread with cancellation, UTF-8 encoding, and temporary directories. One unit test (`test_ParameterArgList`) has a minor bug where assertions still look for old single-dash CLI flags (`-cpu`, `-model_instance`, `-model_labeling`) after `Parameter.asArgList` switched to double-dash flags.

utility.rationale: Inspected `README.md` and `SlicerSPINEPS/SlicerSPINEPS.py`. The extension provides well-documented whole-spine MRI and CT segmentation (both vertebra instance and subregion masks), clear offline weight instructions, validation notes, and clinical disclaimers.

findings.title: PyTorch installed directly via light-the-torch instead of the Slicer PyTorch extension
findings.evidence:
if not self.isPackageInstalled("light-the-torch"):
            self._log("Installing light-the-torch (selects the right PyTorch build)...")
            self.pip_install(LIGHT_THE_TORCH_REQUIREMENT)

        backend = "CUDA" if self.isCudaGpuAvailable() else "CPU"
        self._log(
            f"Downloading PyTorch ({backend} build, this is a large download and may "
            "take several minutes)..."
        )
        slicer.util._executePythonModule("light_the_torch", ["install", *TORCH_PACKAGES])
findings.explanation: The Slicer Extensions Index review policy explicitly requires PyTorch to be installed through the Slicer PyTorch extension (`PyTorchUtils`, listed in `build_dependencies` and `EXTENSION_DEPENDS`) rather than via direct use of `light-the-torch`. Additionally, the catalog entry has `"build_dependencies": []` and `CMakeLists.txt` has `set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA")`. While the author's design rationale (avoiding an extra extension install, Slicer restart, and importing `torch` into the main Slicer process on Windows) and the care taken to reuse existing PyTorch installations and pin core packages (`SimpleITK`, `numpy`, `scipy`, `torch`, `nnunetv2`) are well-reasoned, bypassing the `PyTorch` extension directly conflicts with the Extensions Index policy for managing Slicer's shared Python environment.
findings.suggestion: Declare `PyTorch` (and optionally `NNUNet` if sharing its install logic) in `EXTENSION_DEPENDS` in `CMakeLists.txt` and `build_dependencies` in `SPINEPS.json`, and use `PyTorchUtils` to manage PyTorch installation in accordance with Slicer Extensions Index policy.

findings.title: Unit test `test_ParameterArgList` checks outdated CLI flag names and will fail
findings.evidence:
# The CT semantic model has its own instance and labeling models. SPINEPS' own
        # "sample" command does not pair them (only "dataset" resolves "auto"), and it
        # accepts a mismatch silently, so selecting "ct" must switch all three.
        ctArgs = Parameter(semanticModel="ct").asArgList(Path("/tmp/x.nii.gz"))
        self.assertEqual(ctArgs[ctArgs.index("-model_instance") + 1], "ct_instance")
        self.assertEqual(ctArgs[ctArgs.index("-model_labeling") + 1], "ct_labeling")
findings.explanation: `Parameter.asArgList` was updated for SPINEPS >= 2.1.1 to emit double-dash hyphenated flags (`--model-semantic`, `--model-instance`, `--model-labeling`, `--cpu`), and line 395 of `test_ParameterArgList` was updated to check `--model-semantic`. However, lines 397, 413, and 414 of `test_ParameterArgList` still check for the old single-dash flags (`-cpu`, `-model_instance`, `-model_labeling`), which causes `SlicerSPINEPSTest.test_ParameterArgList` to fail with a `ValueError` when the self-test runs.
findings.suggestion: Update `test_ParameterArgList` in `SlicerSPINEPS/SlicerSPINEPS.py` to assert `"--cpu"`, `"--model-instance"`, and `"--model-labeling"` instead of `"-cpu"`, `"-model_instance"`, and `"-model_labeling"`.

not_checked: Runtime execution in 3D Slicer and live PyPI package resolution/download behavior.
External SPINEPS GitHub release payloads (model weights downloaded at first inference run).
questions_for_author: Would you be able to switch PyTorch management to use the standard `PyTorch` Slicer extension (`PyTorchUtils` and `EXTENSION_DEPENDS` / `build_dependencies`), or coordinate with Slicer core maintainers if out-of-process installation should be upstreamed to `PyTorchUtils`?
